title: Protocol for imaging nuclear pore complexes on isolated nuclei of zebrafish early embryos by field emission scanning electron microscopy
protocol: Remove the divider for fish mating.
Exchange water with fresh system water to remove excrement in the bottom tank.
Prepare an equal number of alternative bottom tanks filled with fresh water for transferring inner tanks.
Remove the dividers from all tanks quickly, and set a timer of 15 min for egg collection.
Collect eggs in batches at 15-min intervals.
Transfer all inner tanks to the alternative bottom tanks once the 15-min time is up.
Set the next 15-min timer immediately.
Pour most water and leave about 35 mL of water to drown eggs after fertilization.
Gently pour the eggs into a 100-mm dish, accommodating up to 1000 eggs per dish.
Mark each dish with the spawning time, fish strain, approximate number of eggs, date, and owner’s name.
Exchange the water in the dishes with Holtfreter’s solution.
Incubate the dishes at 28.5°C.
Repeat the above steps for 2 or 3 times once the next 15-minute timer is up.
Pool different batches of embryos when they reach a matchable developmental stage.
Control fertilization time by managing divider removal to collect embryos at different stages simultaneously.
Collect zebrafish early embryos with chorion detached at desired stages under a microscope.
Monitor embryonic development according to classical definitions and developmental times at 28.5°C.
Pick out unfertilized eggs, abnormal, or degraded embryos in advance.
Prepare the next batch of fertilized eggs when the previous one is in centrifugation, standing, or at a pause point.
Collect embryos from different batches with a 15-minute interval to maintain the same developmental stage.
Transfer collected embryos to a suitable dish, such as a 35-mm dish for about 2000 embryos.
Aspirate excess Holtfreter’s solution until only a minimal level remains while keeping the embryos submerged.
Add pronase stock solution at 30 mg/mL into the Holtfreter’s solution to achieve a final concentration of approximately 1 mg/mL.
Incubate the embryos at 28.5°C for about 7 minutes.
Fill the dish with Holtfreter’s solution to dilute and wash out the reaction mixture when chorions of about one-third of the embryos are broken.
Stop pronase digestion once partial chorions are detached from embryos.
Wash embryos with Holtfreter’s solution for two or more times.
Transfer the embryos to a 1.5-mL EP tube on ice after confirming that most embryos have reached the desired stage under a microscope.
Deyolk zebrafish early embryos, transferring no more than 500 embryos into one 1.5-mL EP tube.
Aspirate the Holtfreter’s solution.
Wash embryos twice with ice-cold Ringer’s solution.
Add ice-cold Ringer’s solution containing final 1× protease inhibitor cocktail to each EP tube to a final volume of 1 mL.
Add 67 μL of 8% PFA to each EP tube to achieve a final concentration of about 0.5% PFA.
Pipette up and down gently with a 1-mL tip to disrupt yolk.
Transfer 10 μL of suspension into a 35-mm dish and examine blastomere cell integrity under a stereomicroscope.
Place the tube lying on the bench top at room temperature for 5 min (starting the timer when PFA is added).
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Gently resuspend the pellet in 1 mL cold Ringer’s solution containing protease inhibitor cocktail with 1-mL tips.
Pellet blastomeres by centrifugation at 500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant with minimal residual just covering the pellet.
Optional: Wash blastomeres with ice-cold Ringer’s solution one more time if the yolk is not removed well.
Gently resuspend the blastomere pellet in 200 μL ice-cold PBS once blastomeres from all batches are collected.
Pool suspensions from up to 5 tubes into one EP tube, and centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate PBS as much as possible.
Add 200 μL ice-cold hypotonic buffer into each tube.
Gently resuspend the pellet by pipetting up and down with a 200-μL tip.
Incubate on ice for 5 min.
Gently pass blastomeres thrice through a 21-G needle connected to the hub of a 1-mL syringe.
Pass the blastomere suspension through a 40-μm cell strainer.
Centrifuge the filtrate at 1,500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Gently resuspend the pellet in 100 μL of PBS + 10% glycerol.
Transfer the cell suspension to 900 μL of PBS + 10% glycerol inside the improvised centrifugation holder.
Put the device inside a conventional 50-mL tube stuffed with facial tissues.
Centrifuge at 800 × g for 10 min at 4°C in a swing-bucket rotor.
Pre-fix nuclei on the silicon chip.
Place silicon chips, with nuclei attached side upwards, in the wells of a 48-well cell culture plate.
Transfer silicon chips between two wells for solution exchange using high precision tweezers.
Remove old solution from the first well and replace it with new solution before transferring the chip again.
Repeat subsequent exchanges by removing some of the old solution and introducing an equal amount of ethanol, gradually increasing the concentration.
Carefully transfer the silicon chip into a 48-well cell culture plate filled with 1 mL PBS for washing.
Transfer the silicon chip to another well in the plate filled with 2% PFA + 2% GA solution.
Fix the silicon chip for 30 minutes at room temperature or overnight at 4°C under dark conditions.
Wash the chip thrice in 0.1 M cacodylate buffer for 2 min each.
Mix an equal volume of ddH2O and 0.2 M cacodylate buffer to achieve a final concentration of 0.1 M.
Post-fix samples in 1% OsO4 in 0.1 M cacodylate buffer for 10 min at room temperature under dark condition.
Transfer the silicon chip to a new 48-well cell culture plate filled with ddH2O and wash for 2 min.
Repeat ddH2O wash for additional two times, 2 min each.
Dehydrate through a graded ethanol series: 30%, 50%, 70%, 90% and 95%, 3 min each, repeat twice for each step.
Transfer the silicon chip to 100% ethanol, 6 × 3 min.
Pause the experiment.
Transfer silicon chip to CPD apparatus filled with ethanol for drying.
Exchange fluid in CPD apparatus with high purity liquid CO2 twelve times.
Convert CO2 to gas under its critical point of specific temperature and pressure.
Process dried samples to sputter coating as soon as possible.
Transfer the silicon chip onto an aluminum stub covered with a carbon adhesive tab.
Transfer the specimen to a sputter-coating apparatus.
Coat the specimens with a 10-nanometre thick gold layer for FESEM imaging.
Image NPCs on the nuclear surface under a FESEM instrument after professional training or with assistance from an instrumental technician.
Discard the supernatant with minimal liquid residual.
Add 500 μL hypertonic sucrose buffer to the pellet.
Gently pipette the pellet using a 200-μL tip for suspension.
Transfer the suspension to the cylinder of a Dounce homogenizer.
Homogenize the suspension in a Dounce homogenizer with the “loose” pestle for 8–10 passes, up and down the cylinder, on ice.
Transfer the homogenate to a 1.5 mL polypropylene ultracentrifuge tube using a 200-μL pipette.
Centrifuge the homogenate at 80,000 × g for 80 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant sucrose buffer as far as possible, especially the residuals on the tube wall.
Resuspend the pellet in 205 μL PBS by gently pipetting using a 200-μL tip.
Transfer the resuspension to a new 1.5-mL EP tube.
Centrifuge 200 μL suspension at 800 × g for 10 min at 4°C to pellet the nuclei.
Discard the supernatant.
Aspirate PBS absolutely, but don’t touch the potential nuclei pellet.
Snap freeze in liquid nitrogen, and store at -80°C for up to 1 month.
Add 5 μL PBS to the remaining 5 μL resuspension to expand the volume.
Stain isolated nuclei with WGA AF647 at a final concentration of 5 μg/mL.
Stain isolated nuclei with DAPI at a final concentration of 1 μg/mL.
Incubate stained nuclei for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Transfer approximately 2 μL of the nuclei suspension into a confocal dish.
Take photos under a confocal microscope for quality check.
Count the number of nuclei with a hemocytometer.
Estimate the total number of collected nuclei based on the whole volume.
Record the location of storage and the number of nuclei for each tube.
Pool different tubes containing the same sample to obtain sufficient nuclei for subsequent mass spectrometry.
Perform mass spectrometry analysis.
